parameters.content:
## Old Photo to Talking Video with Meta Muse

**Who it's for:** families and genealogy fans, memorial and anniversary makers, local-history pages, and creators of "this old photo talks" posts.

It runs on **your own Muse account** through the [useapi.net Muse API](https://useapi.net/docs/api-muse-v1?utm_source=n8n&utm_medium=referral&utm_campaign=muse-photo-app), **a third-party API, not affiliated with Meta**.

**How it works**
1. The form takes a photo (file or link), the restore mode, the line to say, optional motion and voice hints, the format and 1 or 2 takes. The upload is free.
2. **Before you spend** shows the account's live weekly allowance and the estimate.
3. Muse restores (and colorizes) the photo. Use it, redo it with notes, or animate the original.
4. Muse animates the photo and the person says your line: about 10 s with sound. Pick a take or redo with a new line.
5. The result page plays the MP4, links the downloads, shows the % of the week the run used, and can save to Google Drive.

**Errors:** busy and "nothing made" answers are retried. A job that may already have used the allowance is never sent again: it stops with its job id.

**Set up**
1. Get a [useapi.net API token](https://useapi.net/docs/start-here/setup-useapi?utm_source=n8n&utm_medium=referral&utm_campaign=muse-photo-app) and add your Muse account with [Setup Muse](https://useapi.net/docs/start-here/setup-muse?utm_source=n8n&utm_medium=referral&utm_campaign=muse-photo-app).
2. Create a **Header Auth** credential: Name `Authorization`, Value `Bearer <your token>`. Select it on every HTTP Request node.
3. Create a **Basic Auth** credential (any username and password) and select it on **Bring a photo to life**, so only you can open the form and spend your allowance.
4. Publish (activate) the workflow and open the form URL.

**Requirements:** a useapi.net subscription and a Muse account created in the US or Canada (as of October 2026). The free Muse plan works: in our tests a take used about 2-3% of the week and a restore 0-1%.

**Customize:** prompts and the Drive folder are at the top of **Read the form**; batch settings in **Settings**. Code and the sheet template: [GitHub](https://github.com/useapi/muse-api).

### 1. Form + upload
The photo goes to your Muse workspace with **POST /assets**: uploads are free and use no allowance. **Read account** reads the live weekly quota, and **Before you spend** shows it with the estimate before anything is spent. A line over 30 words stops here (a video is about 10 s).

### 2. Restore + pick or redo
**POST /jobs/image** with the photo as `image_1`, polled every 10 s. The prompt keeps the crop and aspect ratio. **Restored** shows before and after: use it, redo with notes, or animate the original. A `403` means Muse refused: its own words come back here with the edit box, never resent unchanged.

### 3. Talking takes
**POST /jobs/video** with the restored photo's assetId as `image_1`: it never leaves Muse. The line in quotes is spoken; the ratio goes in the prompt. 1 or 2 takes run side by side and are polled every 15 s. `429` and `503` (nothing made) are sent again after 30 s; nothing else is. **Your takes** lets you pick one or redo.

### 4. Result + Google Drive
Optional Drive upload of the MP4 and the restored WebP. **Read account (after)** gives the real cost: the % used before and after. Files stay in your Muse workspace until you delete them.

### 5. Stops
A page says what to fix: token (`401`), account (`404`, `596`), allowance (`412`, with the reset time), a bad link (`400`). `500`, `502`, `504` or no answer may already have used the allowance: never resent, the page shows the job id to check.

### 6. Media file (player and downloads)
The pictures, the players and the download links call this webhook. It fetches the file with your credential, so the token never reaches the browser. Each link carries a signed ticket that expires (24 h on the pages, `linkHours` in the sheet); the webhook never takes an assetId or a URL, and answers 404 to anything else.

### 7. Google Sheet batch (off by default)
One row per photo: `photo_url`, `restore`, `notes`, `line`, `motion`, `format`, then the state columns. Every 10 minutes a tick moves each row on: `new` → `restoring` → `check photo`. Type `ok`, `redo: <notes>` or `original` in **status** to go on → `rendering` → `done`. The jobid is written into the row before the next tick, so a restart never pays twice. Copy the columns from `n8n/old-photos-sheet.csv` in the repo, set **Settings**, connect Google Sheets, then enable the trigger.
